title: Sam Bradford's 2008 Heisman: 50 TD Passes and a Close Vote
question: How many touchdowns did Sam Bradford throw in his 2008 Heisman season?
answer: Sam Bradford threw 50 touchdown passes for 4,720 yards in 2008, counting the national title game, and won that year's Heisman Trophy as a redshirt sophomore.
summary: Oklahoma City's Sam Bradford threw 50 TD passes in 2008 and won the Heisman over Colt McCoy and Tim Tebow, then went No. 1 overall in the 2010 NFL draft.
body: Sam Bradford was a hometown hero in the truest sense. Born in Oklahoma City, he starred in football, basketball and golf at Putnam City North and was a three-star recruit when he committed to OU in December 2005. After redshirting in 2006, he led the nation in passing efficiency as a redshirt freshman in 2007.

Then came 2008. Bradford led the nation in passing, throwing for 4,720 yards and 50 touchdowns over the full season as the Sooners reached the BCS national championship game. Oklahoma fell to Florida 24-14 in that game and finished 12-2.

The Heisman race that year was a three-way thriller. Florida's Tim Tebow actually drew the most first-place votes, 309 to Bradford's 300, and Texas' Colt McCoy was right there too. Bradford won on the strength of 315 second-place votes, finishing with 1,726 points to McCoy's 1,604 and Tebow's 1,575. He became the fifth Sooner to win the trophy and also took home the Davey O'Brien Award.
Bradford is a citizen of the Cherokee Nation, and he became the second person of Native American descent to win the Heisman, following Jim Plunkett.

A shoulder injury cut short his 2009 season, but the St. Louis Rams still made him the first overall pick of the 2010 NFL draft, and he was named Offensive Rookie of the Year. He went on to start for the Eagles and Vikings before a final season with Arizona in 2018.
